Around the stand

What it looks like when you roll up

The park

There's a whole park behind the window

Most espresso stands are a box in a parking lot. This one built a park around itself and hung a sign on the gate that says thank you for visiting.

A timber gazebo with a metal roof, a carved salmon strung from the rafters, red patio tables in the sun and more of them in the shade, rope fence along the lawn, and enough room to lean half a dozen bikes. Out at the road, a coffee mug the size of a barrel, carved out of a stump.

It sits where the Foothills Trail runs through South Prairie, which is why the regulars show up in cycling shoes. One of them put it best on Yelp: his drink is usually already made by the time he gets to the window.

In their own words

What people actually say

Getting there

Roll up to the window

  1. Come off the trail or off the highway

    Bikes and boots come in from the Foothills Trail side; cars pull into the lot beside the stand.

  2. Order at the walk-up window

    Espresso, blended, a burrito off the Burrito Bros list, or a candy bar in a cup.

  3. Stay a while

    Take it under the gazebo. Shade on one side, sun on the other, and room for the bike.
